paper_title: LaSQuE Improved Zero-Shot Classification from Explanations Through   Quantifier Modeling and Curriculum Learning
caption: Classification accuracy on novel real-world classification tasks in .
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates classification accuracy on novel real-world classification tasks for several methods, shown as a single series of six vertical bars. The horizontal axis contains the method categories (not printed as x‑tick labels but indicated by the legend) in the displayed left-to-right order: “RoBERTa w/o Exp.”, “ExEnt”, “LaSQuE (mean)”, “LaSQuE”, “LaSQuE (syn2real)”, and “LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum)”. The vertical axis is labeled “Accuracy (%)” and uses a linear percent scale with labeled ticks at approximately 40%, 45%, 50%, 55%, 60%, and 65% (regular 5% intervals), with horizontal dashed gridlines aligned to these ticks. The bars are color-coded to match the legend: a light gray bar for “RoBERTa w/o Exp.” at roughly 46–47%, a light blue bar for “ExEnt” at about 55%, an orange bar for “LaSQuE (mean)” at about 47%, a green bar for “LaSQuE” also around 47%, a purple bar for “LaSQuE (syn2real)” at roughly 59%, and a dark gray bar for “LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum)” at about 62%. The bars are not stacked or grouped beyond being placed side-by-side, and there are no visible annotations or special emphasis beyond the distinct fill colors and the legend.
